title: Odyssey-3 is a new generative world model that you can try for free
key_facts: California-based Odyssey has launched a public research preview of its world model Odyssey-3; users generate interactive environments from text prompts and explore them in real time, and developers can apply for API access.
The free online demo runs on Odyssey-3 Flash; the base model has 14 billion parameters and generates 832 x 480 video, while Odyssey-3 Pro supports 1280 x 720.

Odyssey says Odyssey-3 Pro scores 66.1 on the Physics-IQ Verified video-to-video benchmark, but that score comes from a single run in which a selection method picked one of eight generated videos per task.

The benchmark rules require four runs with standard deviation reported for any record claim; without the selection method, Odyssey-3 Pro averaged 63.37 across four runs. Both results are on the official leaderboard but were submitted by Odyssey itself.
On the WorldMark benchmark, by Odyssey's own evaluation, Odyssey-3 ranks first in three of four categories and third in First-Person Real (80.6).

Odyssey says controllers built on Odyssey-3 operated robot arms, a drone in a virtual indoor space and a GTA V game character, and it works with Swiss robotics company Flexion on humanoids; all of these are company-reported.
The public preview offers interactive environment generation for now; robotics and autonomous systems will need further work.
Founders Oliver Cameron and Jeff Hawke first unveiled the model on 15 Sep; Odyssey raised $310 million in June 2026 from investors including Amazon and AMD Ventures.
